xcart_same_env._superseded: Superseded by controlled_xcart_ab. Retained for DIRECTION only — magnitudes unusable: SQL per GetFullCart also fell 78% (50.18 -> 10.99), which this fix cannot cause, indicating different workloads between the windows; and vcst-qa is continuously redeployed.

total_dependency_count._note: Literal reading of Oleg's criterion 1 — ALL dependencies per request, not just product _search. Same corrected windows.
total_dependency_count._invalidating_finding: SQL deps per GetFullCart fell 78% (50.18 -> 10.99). VCST-5637 dedups Elasticsearch product searches and touches NO SQL — each caller still gets a clone and still runs its own downstream pricing/inventory work. A 78% SQL drop cannot be caused by this fix. Most likely the before and after populations are different workloads (cart size drives both SQL and ES counts ~linearly; before n=33 dominated by a large-cart regression run, after n=79 mostly small carts). CONCLUSION: Measurement 2 magnitudes are NOT trustworthy and GetFullCart's 597->129ms is better explained by 39 fewer SQL round-trips than by 5.5 fewer ES searches.

controlled_xcart_ab._design: identical cart (3 line items x qty 2) + byte-identical query text on both envs, 1 VU, 0% overlap. before=vcptcore-qa XCatalog 3.1014.0, after=vcst-qa 3.1016.0-pr-106.

es_product_search_per_cart_request.note: after side tight at 3-4 across 6 observations (all unsampled in replication 2); before side wider at 6-10, reflecting cache state and read-vs-write mix

total_deps_same_requests.note: in-band — SQL side unchanged, the correct signature for an Elasticsearch-only change and the check that rules out crediting this fix with an unrelated improvement

controlled_xcart_ab.product_caveat: products necessarily differ between catalogs — vcptcore-qa has ZERO tracked inventory so only isTrackInventory=false products are addable there; cart SHAPE is identical, which is what the count comparison requires
controlled_xcart_ab.cache_confound: vcptcore-qa is idle (cold platform caches) where vcst-qa carries continuous traffic, so warm caches could in principle explain part of the gap. In replication 2 vcptcore-qa's caches were already warm from the preceding runs and it still measured 6-10 vs 3-4 — this weakens the alternative explanation but does not eliminate it. The catalog distinct-criteria arm carries the decisive control.

methodological_findings: Repeated identical requests are NOT independent samples: 8 identical cart reads collapsed from 6 searches/317ms to 1 search/10ms within seconds ON THE PRE-FIX BUILD — the platform's own catalog caches warming, not this fix. Only the cold request discriminates; a naive repeat-and-average would have reported the fix as doing nothing.

App Insights adaptive sampling retained 3 of 11 requests per arm (itemCount 2-4). Each retained record is one real request with real dependency counts and shares its multiplier with its dependencies, so per-request integrity holds; both arms sampled alike.
scope_for_test.criterion_2_durations: NOT CLAIMED — cross-env latency is out of scope by the ticket's own stated boundary, and the same-env duration data is workload-confounded (AddCoupon median rose 421->555ms). Only dependency COUNTS are claimed.
